newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee roasters seen covered until June.
newsitem.headline: German coffee roasters seen covered until June.

text.p: German coffee roasters have taken raw materials cover for the next 10 weeks and trade and household supplies also look comfortable, traders said.
"It's fairly quiet now and most industry buyers are quite relaxed after New York futures ended only modestly higher on Friday," one said.
"But consumers are aware of a possibly supply tightness in the second half of 1997 -- in July/August/September ahead of new crop arrivals."
Traders also said cooler weather in Brazil's coffee belt, which prompted some buying in New York last Friday, looked unlikely to bring damaging frost.
But it had shown the market had moved into the unforeseeable time of year when Brazil weather news can create instant volatility.
This should support the New York May contract, perhaps in a 180-215 cents/lb range in the near future, one said.
New York May arabicas ended at 179.15 cents last Friday, up 1.45, and July settled 1.40 higher at 164.75.
Retail price increases, which roasters said in February they would enforce by raising ex-plant prices on March 10, were now beginning to materialise, according to retail sector observers.
Increases by two to four marks per kilo of roasted coffee were being implemented by major food store chains, they said.
In the import market, outright purchases of Central Americans and some Colombians were reported amid lower prices.
Brazil prices held relatively firm and African arabica grades also remained expensive while robustas were neglected.

Brazils were at $193 per 50 kg fob, off $1 on the past fortnight, Colombians at $220, off $10, and Vietnam robustas were off $6.50 per 50 kg cif at $70.0. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom +49-40-41903275
